elicitation_input.question: In relation to spiritual diety Pachamama, in 2011 Bolivia announced an new unusual Law of what?

llm_generation.text:
In 2011, Bolivia announced a new "Law of Mother Earth" (Ley de Derechos de la Madre Tierra), which was groundbreaking legislation that granted nature—Pachamama, the Andean earth goddess—legal rights equivalent in some respects to those of humans.

The law recognized the Earth as a living system with rights, including:
- The right to life and to exist
- The right to continue vital cycles and processes free from human alteration
- The right to pure water and clean air
- The right to balance
- The right to not be polluted
- The right to not have cellular structure modified or genetically altered

This legislation was significant as it reflected the indigenous Andean worldview, where Pachamama (Mother Earth) is considered a sacred, living entity deserving of respect and protection, rather than simply a resource for human exploitation. Bolivia's move was seen as part of a broader push by the country, under President Evo Morales, to incorporate indigenous cosmovision into national policy and to position itself as a leader in environmental and indigenous rights advocacy on the global stage.
